# Whether cursor's agent backend will call a tool a third-party client declares,
# and what that client may do while it holds one open.
#
# The recording W3's gate reads (.omc/plans/2026-09-04-cursor-tool-bridge.md, W2
# step 5; AC-7 and AC-8). Five live turns against api2.cursor.sh, each run by the
# user through `!` — no lane and no lead ran one, and nothing here was read out of
# auth.json. What the wire itself said is in the run's own log at `-v`; the line
# numbers below are that file's.
#
# Recorded by: the W2 spike scaffolding,
#              crates/ganja-provider/src/provider/cursor/spike.rs — environment-
#              gated, and removed in W3a or W4 along with this file's subject.
# Build:  ganja-code 0.1.0; ./target/release/ganja rebuilt from f140f20.
# Date:   2026-09-06, 09:40:32 - 09:43:51 UTC (five consecutive `ganja run -v`).
# Log:    ~/.local/share/ganja/log/ganja.2026-09-06.log, 633 lines.
# Server: api2.cursor.sh. This client identified as cli-2026.01.09-231024f, the
#         constant cursor.rs has always sent.
# Spec:   cursor-agent bundle 2026.09.02-c22c1a3, read in
#         .omc/research/cursor/2026-09-04-cursor-agent-bundle-read.md. Every field
#         number below was re-derived from that bundle's own descriptors.
# Model:  GANJA_MODEL unset on all five runs, so the turn ran under cursor's
#         server-side `default` (Auto). Which model that resolved to is decided
#         server-side and is not observable from this client.
#
# What was declared, identically on every run: exactly one tool,
#   McpToolDefinition{ name = 1 "ganja_ping",
#                      description = 2 "Answers pong. A probe.",
#                      provider_identifier = 4 "ganja",
#                      tool_name = 5 "ganja_ping" }
# with {"type":"object","properties":{},"additionalProperties":false} on
# input_schema = 3, input_schema_json = 6, or both, per the run.
# Carried on AgentRunRequest.mcp_tools = 4 (McpTools.mcp_tools = 1) and on every
# RequestContext.tools = 7 answer.
#
# NO CONNECT ERROR OF ANY KIND WAS PRODUCED BY ANY OF THE FIVE RUNS. No `code`,
# no `message`, no EndStream error frame, no truncated body, no auth refusal. The
# plan asks for every error code and message verbatim; the honest verbatim record
# is that there were none, and the sections below say so where the question was
# whether one would appear.

== the runs ==
# One line per run: the environment beyond GANJA_PROVIDER=cursor and
# GANJA_CURSOR_SPIKE=1, the log window, and what the run was for.
R1  SCHEMA=both DELAY_SECS=25                     log :13-:101   (a), (b)
R2  SCHEMA=both DELAY_SECS=25 EXEC_HEARTBEAT=1    log :114-:206  (b')
R3  SCHEMA=3    DELAY_SECS=0  (+ "then read Cargo.toml")
                                                  log :219-:452  (e) field 3, (c)
R4  SCHEMA=6    DELAY_SECS=0                      log :466-:532  (e) field 6
R5  SCHEMA=both DELAY_SECS=0  PROMPT=append       log :545-:630  (d)

# Every run ended by printing a reply and exiting; none emitted a
# ProviderEvent::Failed. The wire logs no line for a clean EndStream, so "the turn
# completed" here means: a reply was printed, the process exited, and no failure
# was reported — not that a "finished" line was found.

== (a) does the server offer and call a client-declared tool ==
VERDICT: YES

The model called the declared tool on R1, R2, R3 and R4 — every run whose prompt
asked for it, under all three schema selectors. R1, log :47:

  cursor spike: mcp exec arrived provider="cursor" exec=1 kind="mcp_args"
    number=11 ganja_ping=true tool_call_id=true provider_identifier=true
    tool_name=true server_identifier=true others=[]

Observed, by field:
  ExecServerMessage.mcp_args = 11        present; the arm the bundle predicted
  ExecServerMessage.id = 1               present, value 1 (the turn's first exec)
  McpArgs.name = 1                       present, equal to the declared name
  McpArgs.tool_call_id = 3               present
  McpArgs.provider_identifier = 4        present
  McpArgs.tool_name = 5                  present
  McpArgs.server_identifier = 9          present
  McpArgs.args = 2                       ABSENT (others=[] — no unknown field
                                         reached the decoder, and this schema
                                         declares no arguments to send)
  McpArgs.smart_mode_approval_only = 7   ABSENT
  McpArgs.skip_approval = 8              ABSENT
  McpArgs.smart_mode_approval = 6        ABSENT

The synthetic provider_identifier "ganja", which names no MCP server that exists,
was accepted: the server echoed identifiers back rather than refusing to resolve
the roster. The answer this client sent — ExecClientMessage.mcp_result = 11
carrying McpResult.success = 1, McpSuccess{content = 1 [McpContentItem.text = 1
McpTextContent{text = 1}], is_error = 2 false}, then
ExecClientControlMessage.stream_close = 1 — was accepted on all four runs; each
model then reported the answered word back to the user (R1 :55, R2 :149, R3 :260,
R4 :488).

Identical `mcp exec arrived` lines with the same field set: R2 :133, R3 :257,
R4 :485.

== (b) does a >= 20 s pause survive on run heartbeats alone ==
VERDICT: YES        delay used: 25 seconds

R1, exec heartbeats OFF. AgentClientMessage.client_heartbeat = 7 (ClientHeartbeat,
fieldless) went out every five seconds and nothing else did. Log :48-:55:

  :48  holding the probe's exec open  exec=1 delay_secs=25 exec_heartbeat=false
  :49  run heartbeat, mid-hold  elapsed_ms=486
  :50  run heartbeat, mid-hold  elapsed_ms=5486
  :51  run heartbeat, mid-hold  elapsed_ms=10485
  :52  run heartbeat, mid-hold  elapsed_ms=15486
  :53  run heartbeat, mid-hold  elapsed_ms=20486
  :54  the hold elapsed         elapsed_ms=25001
  :55  answering the probe with mcp_result.success

(The first tick lands at 486 ms because the interval had been running since the
stream opened; the cadence between ticks is the 5,000 ms it was set to.)

After the answer the same stream carried the server's own kv sets (:56-:66), a
further run heartbeat at :68, thinking and text deltas, and a reply. Nothing was
aborted, nothing was retried, and no error frame arrived. A 25-second client-side
pause inside one exec is survivable on the run-level heartbeat alone.

== (b') does the same pause survive with exec heartbeats on ==
VERDICT: YES        delay used: 25 seconds

R2, the same 25 s hold with GANJA_CURSOR_SPIKE_EXEC_HEARTBEAT=1, so
ExecClientControlMessage.heartbeat = 3 (ExecClientHeartbeat{id = 1}, carrying the
held exec's own id) went out every three seconds beside the five-second run
heartbeat. Log :134-:149:

  :134 holding the probe's exec open  exec=1 delay_secs=25 exec_heartbeat=true
  :136 exec heartbeat  exec=1 elapsed_ms=3002
  :137 exec heartbeat  exec=1 elapsed_ms=6001
  :139 exec heartbeat  exec=1 elapsed_ms=9002
  :140 exec heartbeat  exec=1 elapsed_ms=12002
  :142 exec heartbeat  exec=1 elapsed_ms=15002
  :144 exec heartbeat  exec=1 elapsed_ms=18002
  :145 exec heartbeat  exec=1 elapsed_ms=21001
  :147 exec heartbeat  exec=1 elapsed_ms=24002
  :148 the hold elapsed  exec=1 elapsed_ms=25001
  :149 answering the probe with mcp_result.success

  interleaved run heartbeats at :135 (2211 ms), :138, :141, :143, :146

The server neither required the exec heartbeat nor objected to it: (b) already
passed without it, and the eight extra frames changed nothing observable. This
answers W3's criterion 3 with evidence rather than by assumption — the choice
between the two shapes is cost, not feasibility.

== (c) how a typed `rejected` on a native kind is treated ==
VERDICT: YES — the turn survives, and the model adapts

R3's prompt asked for the probe and then for a file read. After the probe was
served (:257-:260), the server asked for four native execs in a row, each answered
with D550's typed refusal — the kind's own rejected/error arm carrying ganja's
reason — and each followed by the stream close:

  :263  exec arrived  exec=2 kind="read_args"          number=7
  :264  refusing an exec cursor asked this client to run  exec=2 typed=true
  :312  exec arrived  exec=3 kind="shell_stream_args"  number=14
  :313  refusing an exec cursor asked this client to run  exec=3 typed=true
  :350  exec arrived  exec=4 kind="grep_args"          number=5
  :351  refusing an exec cursor asked this client to run  exec=4 typed=true
  :354  exec arrived  exec=5 kind="grep_args"          number=5
  :355  refusing an exec cursor asked this client to run  exec=5 typed=true

`typed=true` on all four means none of them fell back to D486's control-channel
throw. The server's agent loop read each refusal as a tool outcome: it tried a
different kind after each one (read, then a streamed shell, then grep twice),
generated text between the attempts, and finished the turn with a reply that
reported the probe's answer and stated plainly that the file could not be read.
The turn ran on to :452 and ended normally.

This is the confirmation W1's premise needed: a typed rejection on a native kind
does not kill a cursor turn, and W1's step-6 revert is not required.

== (d) is AgentRunRequest.system_prompt_spec = 29 gated ==
VERDICT: IGNORED — neither honored nor refused

R5 sent SystemPromptSpec{append = 2} carrying a marker sentence instructing the
model to begin every reply with a fixed word, beside the ordinary system prompt on
RequestContext.cloud_rule = 16.

What happened: the turn ran normally end to end (:545-:630 — a context ask, kv
sets, thinking deltas, text deltas, step_completed, a reply, clean exit) and the
reply did **not** begin with the marker word or contain it anywhere.

What did NOT happen, which is the load-bearing half: no `invalid_argument`, no
Connect error frame of any code, no refusal message. This is the third outcome the
runbook named, and it is distinct from `custom_system_prompt = 8`'s behaviour,
which LIVE-FAILED an ordinary seat's turn with

  400 invalid_argument: unknown option '--system-prompt'

(the refusal recorded in cursor/request.rs's module doc, not re-observed here).
So field 29 is accepted by the wire and, on this seat and this model, has no
observable effect on the reply. Whether it is silently dropped, allowlist-gated
without an error, or honored in some way this prompt could not detect, is not
settled by one run.

== (e) which schema field the server honored ==
VERDICT: BOTH — field 3 alone works, and field 6 alone works

Three runs, one variable:

  R1/R2  input_schema = 3 AND input_schema_json = 6   tool called  (:47, :133)
  R3     input_schema = 3 only                        tool called  (:257)
  R4     input_schema_json = 6 only                   tool called  (:485)

Neither field is required, and neither is ignored to the point of breaking the
call. The two encodings the spike sent were derived from one JSON string, so a
disagreement between them cannot be what produced this result.

W4 may therefore choose on other grounds. The bundle's own client picks exactly
one (index.js@5699717), and the reference implementation this port's research
cites sends field 3.

== what this cannot measure ==

1. The probe's schema declares NO ARGUMENTS. `others=[]` on every call confirms
   the server sent no McpArgs.args = 2, so nothing here shows that a *populated*
   schema round-trips, that argument values survive the encoding, or that field 3
   and field 6 stay equivalent once a schema has properties in it. (e)'s verdict
   is "the call happened with only this field filled" and not "this field is
   read". A W4 tool with real arguments is what settles that.

2. `provider_identifier` was the synthetic "ganja", naming no MCP server that
   exists. The server accepted it here; nothing says a registry lookup is not
   performed under other conditions, or that a roster of more than one tool, a
   longer description, or a name outside this charset would be accepted. The
   bundle read found no client-side name grammar or count cap and could not rule
   out server-side ones; this run does not rule them out either.

3. One seat, one account, one model (`default`/Auto), one client version, one
   bundle version, one afternoon. Nothing here says what a different tier, an
   explicitly named model, or a later server does. Cursor's own client version
   gating is unexercised: every run identified as cli-2026.01.09-231024f.

4. The hold was measured at 25 seconds. Nothing here bounds where the ceiling is,
   or whether one exists — a longer hold, several concurrent holds, or a hold
   under a slower model are all unmeasured. (b) says 25 s survives; it does not
   say 120 s does.

5. (d)'s "ignored" is a negative about one prompt on one model. A model that
   simply declined to follow a formatting instruction would leave the same trace
   as a field the server dropped. Distinguishing those needs a marker the model
   cannot plausibly ignore, or a second channel to compare against.

6. Turn completion is inferred from a printed reply, a clean exit and the absence
   of any ProviderEvent::Failed. This build logs no line for a clean EndStream
   frame, so no positive record of the stream's own verdict exists in the log.

== incidental, and worth knowing before W4 ==

* `ganja run` constructs the cursor wire TWICE per invocation. The second
  `cursor spike: enabled` line in each run (:102, :207, :453, :533, :631) lands at
  process teardown, immediately after the reply, and is a CursorWire::from_stored
  that sent no run request in any of the five runs — the title/summary one-shot,
  built and then dropped as the process exits. It read the same environment and
  would have declared the same tool had it opened a stream. Two consequences for
  W4: a roster is declared per *wire*, not per session, and any per-turn cost of
  declaring one is paid on that path too.

* The context ask (`request_context_args = 10`) arrived with ExecRequest.id
  ABSENT on all five runs (:15, :115, :220, :468, :547 — no `exec=` field), while
  every tool exec carried one, numbered from 1 upward within the turn. The context
  answer echoes what it was given, which is nothing, and the server has never
  objected.

* Both `grep_args` execs on R3 arrived within 5 ms of each other (:350, :354) and
  were refused independently. The server issues concurrent execs; a W4 bridge must
  not assume one outstanding exec at a time.

* The server's kv channel is busy on these turns — dozens of set exchanges per
  run, one of them 185,582 bytes on R5 — all answered from the per-turn blob store
  W1 already ships. No get preceded a set in any run.
